Security forces have launched a counter-operation in the area.
Quick Reaction Teams (QRTs) have also reached the spot.

Choudhury submitted his nomination at the Sabha’s central office, Bhagawati Prasad Barua Bhawan, in Guwahati.

He arrived at the office in a convoy of around 10 vehicles, accompanied by representatives of various branches of the Assam Sahitya Sabha and literary enthusiasts from different districts across the state.

stories.headline: India Launches Anti-Dumping Probe into Aluminium Extrusions, with Solar Mounting Structures in Scope
stories.title: India Launches Anti-Dumping Probe into Aluminium Extrusions, with Solar Mounting Structures in Scope
stories.summary: India's trade remedies authority has opened an anti-dumping investigation into imports of aluminium extrusion products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand. The scope explicitly includes solar mounting structures, which could matter for the cost of solar projects across the country. The investigation covers "Aluminium Extrusion Profiles, Structures and Articles thereof" originating in or exported from the four countries. Four countries, about 90% of imports According to the notification, imports of the subject goods from China PR, Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand increased during the period of investigation. Together, these countries accounted for about 90% of India's total imports of the product. The Authority noted prima facie evidence that the domestic industry has suffered injury. Dumped imports were found to be undercutting domestic prices, resulting in a significant decline in profitability and losses. The industry is also facing falling cash profits, lower return on capital employed and significant underutilisation of capacity. The Authority added that complete information on the impact on economic parameters is not yet available. On dumping, the Authority said the estimated margins are above de minimis. Since price and cost data from the exporting countries were not available at this stage, normal value was constructed from the cost of production of three domestic producers, adjusted for reasonable profit and selling, general and administrative expenses. For China, producers can still seek to show that market economy conditions prevail in the industry. Export prices were derived from transaction-wise import data and adjusted to an ex-factory level. Why solar developers should pay attention The product scope goes well beyond raw profiles, bars, rods and tubes. It also covers articles made predominantly from aluminium extrusions, and the list expressly names solar mounting structures , alongside heat sinks, LED and lighting profiles, industrial T-slot framing, ladders, furniture and bicycle parts. Doors, windows, curtain-wall and façade systems are also included. The Authority's reasoning is that structures and articles are made from extruded profiles through incremental processes such as cutting, machining, welding or joining, and need no additional raw material or primary process. For initiation, they have therefore been treated as part of one product under consideration. The Authority has said the scope will be examined further after comments from interested parties. For solar, this means module mounting structure suppliers, EPC companies and developers that import aluminium structures, or depend on imported extrusions, could be affected if duties are eventually recommended and imposed. Key details of the investigation Period of investigation: 1 April 2025 to 30 June 2026 (15 months). The Authority chose this longer period because the largely MSME domestic producers maintain records on a financial-year basis. Injury period: FY2022-23, FY2023-24, FY2024-25 and the period of investigation. Unit of measurement: Metric tonnes. Tariff classification: Chapter 76 items including 7604, 7608, 7610 and 7616 99 90. The Authority has said the classification is indicative only and does not bind the scope. PCN methodology: No Product Control Number methodology has been proposed at this stage. What It Means for India's Solar Push India is building solar capacity at pace toward its 2030 goal of 500 GW of non-fossil power capacity, and every project needs mounting structures, whether on rooftops, canals or utility-scale ground-mount sites. Structures are a small slice of project cost compared with modules, but they are a visible and fast-moving part of the balance of the system, where developers and EPC firms compete hard on margins. If duties are eventually imposed, the effect will depend on how much of India's demand is met by imported extrusions and structures versus domestic fabricators, and that is exactly what the investigation should bring out. There is a fair case on both sides. Domestic extruders, mostly MSMEs, say dumped imports are eroding their prices and capacity utilisation, and a healthy local extrusion base supports the "Make in India" objective across solar and other sectors. At the same time, developers operating on thin tariffs have little room to absorb higher input costs, and a duty that touches downstream structures could squeeze them or slow rooftop and small-project rollouts. The overlap with the existing duty on solar module frames adds a further layer of trade-protection to the supply chain. The key test will be whether the final scope is drawn narrowly enough to protect domestic producers without adding avoidable cost to the energy transition. Solar developers, structure makers and importers should engage with the process early, because the window to raise scope concerns is only 15 days from the intimation letters.

stories.title: Supreme Court Monthly Roundup: September 2026

article_sentences: Case Details: Anil Singh @ Anil Kumar Singh.
State of Bihar & Ors.

The Supreme Court cautioned the trial courts to proceed with alacrity during trial, especially when there is a total failure of the prosecution for not conducting examination of the crucial witnesses.
“…when there is total failure of the prosecution, the Court should with alacrity question the prosecution's conduct in not examining crucial witnesses.

The Trial Court is not a moot spectator and even in the role of an unbiased adjudicator has the responsibility to ensure that the best evidence is not suppressed by the prosecution…”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the concurrent findings of the Patna High Court and Trial Court's order rejecting the de-facto complainant Section 311 Cr.P.C. application seeking examination of the crucial witness which could have a direct impact on the outcome of the trial.
The case arose from an altercation in which the appellant and his father sustained injuries.
Case Details: Ummed Devi.
State of Rajasthan and Anr.
The Supreme Court has disapproved of dismissing appeals on technical grounds like the absence of a delay condonation application when the litigant was not having proper legal assistance.
It is the duty of the Courts to ensure quality legal assistance to the litigants.

“True that the appeal should have been accompanied with an application for condonation of delay, but the Constitutional Courts should also be alive to the travails of a litigant and if the legal assistance is not adequate, it has a duty to provide quality legal assistance to the litigants, whether it be a victim or an accused.”, observed a bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran, while setting aside the Rajasthan High Court's decision which had dismissed the appeal against an acquittal in a dowry death case merely for want of an application seeking condonation of delay with an appeal.
The victim's mother filed the appeal against the accused's acquittal before the High Court with a 19-day delay.

stories.headline: Perception That One High Court Is Better For A Particular Dispute Is Misguided : Supreme Court Transfers IP Suit From Delhi To Madras
stories.title: Perception That One High Court Is Better For A Particular Dispute Is Misguided : Supreme Court Transfers IP Suit From Delhi To Madras
stories.summary: "The mere existence of territorial jurisdiction in various courts cannot on its own become justification for forum shopping and cannot result in the perpetuation of notions of a hierarchy among the High Courts of this country."
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "The mere existence of territorial jurisdiction in various courts cannot on its own become justification for forum shopping and cannot result in the perpetuation of notions of a hierarchy among the High Courts of this country."

The Supreme Court has observed that the perception that a particular High Court is better suited to adjudicate certain types of disputes, particularly intellectual property disputes, is “entirely misguided and erroneous,” cautioning against forum shopping and notions of hierarchy among High Courts.

A bench of Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice R Mahadevan made the observation while transferring a commercial suit pending before the Delhi High Court to the Madras High Court, noting that the parties to the dispute were carrying on business in neighbouring States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

“While it could be true that various High Courts may have the jurisdiction to hear a particular case, especially in the case of intellectual property disputes, any perception of a particular High Court being better suited to hearing a particular type of dispute is entirely misguided and erroneous.

We also wish to highlight that, ordinarily, in a case whose respective parties, genesis and factual locus are based in a particular location, the courts of the said location would be most suited to understanding the nuances of that case.”
The Court noted that the petitioners carry on business at Chennai, while the respondents (plaintiffs) have their principal place of business at Nelmangala, Bangalore Rural District, Karnataka.

“We fail to understand as to why the respondents/plaintiffs have filed the suit before the Delhi High Court when both the parties are residing in the neighbouring States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and the Madras High Court also has original jurisdiction to entertain the suit.”
“We therefore, find that the petitioner has made out a case for transfer of the suit from the Delhi High Court to the Madras High Court.

We also find that the interests of justice would be served in the instant case, having regard to the fact that the parties are carrying on their respective businesses in the neighbouring States of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and therefore for the expediency of disposal and bearing in mind all practical aspects, the Transfer Petition is liable to be allowed.”
“Accordingly, the Transfer Petition is allowed and the case viz., CS(COMM) 625/2026 on the file of the High Court of Delhi at New Delhi is transferred to the High Court of Judicature at Madras.”

stories.headline: Savitribai Phule Pune University Floats Tender for 1 MWp Rooftop Solar With 5 MWh BESS
stories.title: Savitribai Phule Pune University Floats Tender for 1 MWp Rooftop Solar With 5 MWh BESS
stories.summary: Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU), Maharashtra, has invited bids for installing a 1 MWp rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system integrated with a 5 MWh battery energy storage system ( BESS ) across various buildings on its campus. The project will be implemented under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) model. The tender was published on November 6, 2026. Bids can be submitted until November 30, 2026, at 3 PM, with the opening scheduled for December 1. According to the tender, the scope includes the supply, erection, testing and commissioning of the rooftop-mounted solar PV system and battery storage infrastructure. The project comprises 1,000 kWp of solar capacity and 5,000 kWh of battery storage. 25-year RESCO arrangement Under the RESCO model, the developer is responsible for installing and operating the renewable energy system, while the consumer purchases the electricity generated under an agreed commercial arrangement. The tender specifies a 25-year period for electricity generation and supply from the rooftop solar and BESS project. This arrangement allows the university to procure renewable electricity without necessarily undertaking the entire upfront capital investment for the installation. The tender's bill of quantities (BOQ) also lists a rate of ₹32 per kWh for electricity generated and supplied through the project over the 25-year period. This is a quoted BOQ rate and should not be confused with a final awarded tariff. Eligibility and bidding requirements The university has specified technical qualification requirements for prospective bidders. These include experience in executing a single similar project of at least 1,500 kWp during the last five financial years, along with cumulative project execution experience of at least 3,000 kWp during the same period. Bidders must also demonstrate experience in installing at least one battery energy storage system with a capacity of 500 kWh. The tender carries an earnest money deposit (EMD) of ₹10 lakh and a tender fee of ₹10,000. The bid validity period is 120 days. Universities expand campus solar installations SPPU's proposed project comes amid wider solar adoption across India's higher education institutions, with universities and IITs increasingly using campus rooftops and available land to generate electricity and reduce dependence on grid power. IIT Roorkee, for instance, has reported a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 2.8 MWp, including a 1 MWp plant installed under the RESCO model. Its solar installations cover 27 departmental and institutional buildings. Similarly, IIT Kanpur's Sustainability Report 2024-25 puts its existing solar generation capacity at 2.21 MW, comprising 1 MW under the CAPEX model and 1.21 MW under RESCO. The institute is also installing an additional 0.4 MW system and has assessed the potential to expand its solar capacity to 10 MW. IIT Guwahati signed an agreement with ICICI Foundation in February 2026 to establish a 2 MW solar power plant on its campus. Meanwhile, IIM Bangalore's rooftop solar installation is expected to meet approximately 15% of the institute's electricity requirements. The trend extends beyond the IIT system. Jindal Global University reported 2.4 MW of on-site solar capacity and generated 25.56 lakh kWh of solar electricity in 2025, more than double its 2024 generation of 11.82 lakh kWh. For SPPU, integrating a 5 MWh BESS with rooftop solar introduces another dimension to campus energy management. While solar installations help institutions generate electricity locally, battery storage can shift some of that generation to periods when sunlight is unavailable. However, the project's eventual contribution will depend on its battery power rating, operating schedule, energy procurement arrangement and actual utilisation. Its implementation could offer a useful reference for other large institutional consumers considering solar-plus-storage installations.

These include experience in executing a single similar project of at least 1,500 kWp during the last five financial years, along with cumulative project execution experience of at least 3,000 kWp during the same period.
Bidders must also demonstrate experience in installing at least one battery energy storage system with a capacity of 500 kWh.
The tender carries an earnest money deposit (EMD) of ₹10 lakh and a tender fee of ₹10,000.
The bid validity period is 120 days.

Universities expand campus solar installations SPPU's proposed project comes amid wider solar adoption across India's higher education institutions, with universities and IITs increasingly using campus rooftops and available land to generate electricity and reduce dependence on grid power.
IIT Roorkee, for instance, has reported a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 2.8 MWp, including a 1 MWp plant installed under the RESCO model.
Its solar installations cover 27 departmental and institutional buildings.
Similarly, IIT Kanpur's Sustainability Report 2024-25 puts its existing solar generation capacity at 2.21 MW, comprising 1 MW under the CAPEX model and 1.21 MW under RESCO.
The institute is also installing an additional 0.4 MW system and has assessed the potential to expand its solar capacity to 10 MW.
IIT Guwahati signed an agreement with ICICI Foundation in February 2026 to establish a 2 MW solar power plant on its campus.
The trend extends beyond the IIT system.
Jindal Global University reported 2.4 MW of on-site solar capacity and generated 25.56 lakh kWh of solar electricity in 2025, more than double its 2024 generation of 11.82 lakh kWh.
For SPPU, integrating a 5 MWh BESS with rooftop solar introduces another dimension to campus energy management.
While solar installations help institutions generate electricity locally, battery storage can shift some of that generation to periods when sunlight is unavailable.
However, the project's eventual contribution will depend on its battery power rating, operating schedule, energy procurement arrangement and actual utilisation.
Its implementation could offer a useful reference for other large institutional consumers considering solar-plus-storage installations.

stories.headline: India garment makers rethink reliance on US after tariff shock
stories.title: India garment makers rethink reliance on US after tariff shock
stories.summary: Orient Craft cuts US share from 84% to under 10%; Gokaldas targets Europe as India-UK deal opens duty-free access
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: At Orient Craft’s factory in Ranchi, hundreds of women stitch dresses, shirts and children’s clothing for British retailers Next and Marks & Spencer.
Not long ago, most of Orient Craft’s output would have gone to the US.
But founder Sudhir Dhingra, 77, has cut shipments there since the US hiked tariffs, which rose to as much as 50 per cent last year, hitting orders from customers including American Eagle and Gap.
Even with duties now lower and the possibility of a trade pact, Dhingra has decided it is too much of a risk to depend so heavily on one market.
“Even if there is a deal, what is the guarantee that it will hold water?” he said.
“I don’t wish to see that sword on my head.”

Orient Craft is one of many Indian companies reconfiguring their export destinations, and their exposure to the US, in light of the tariff shock, in a move that is likely to strengthen New Delhi’s hand in its trade negotiations with Washington, and potentially reduce India’s vulnerability to US pressure over time.

Dhingra said US buyers cancelled orders or sought discounts after US President Donald Trump first announced the tariff hikes in April 2025, with some asking suppliers to absorb 25 per cent of the duty, despite manufacturers’ margins being less than 10 per cent.
Orient Craft has since moved sales to Britain, Europe and, to a lesser extent, India.
The US now accounts for less than 10 per cent of sales, down from 84 per cent before the tariffs, with annual exports of about ₹150 crore ($15.82 million).
US duties on Indian products are currently 10 per cent under Section 301, a US law allowing tariffs on imports, as well as base tariffs from 6 per cent to 12 per cent.
Gokaldas Exports, which employs more than 53,000 people and is one of India’s biggest garment exporters, is turning to Europe.

stories.headline: Fresh snowfall in Peer Ki Gali, Gurez; Mughal Road closed ahead of major snow spell in J&K
stories.title: Fresh snowfall in Peer Ki Gali, Gurez; Mughal Road closed ahead of major snow spell in J&K
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 11 : Fresh snowfall was reported at Peer Ki Gali along the Mughal Road and in Gurez Valley on Wednesday, prompting authorities to suspend traffic on the strategic road and restrict tourist movement in vulnerable areas ahead of a major spell of rain and snowfall forecast across Jammu and Kashmir from November 12 to 14. Officials said the Mughal Road, which connects south Kashmir with Rajouri and Poonch districts, was closed for vehicular movement following light rain and snowfall in the Peer Ki Gali area. Deputy Superintendent of Police Traffic, Rajouri-Poonch Range, Ajaz Ahmed Choudhury, said the closure was ordered as a precautionary measure due to slippery road conditions. Commuters have been advised to avoid travelling on the route until further clearance and remain in touch with traffic control rooms for updates. Gurez Valley in north Kashmir also received fresh snowfall, covering parts of the area in a white blanket, as the district administration had already advised tourists against visiting the valley in view of the impending weather conditions. The Meteorological Centre Srinagar has forecast widespread rainfall in the plains and moderate to heavy snowfall in higher reaches during the three-day period, with some mountainous areas likely to receive one to two feet of snow. Speaking to news agency Kashmir News Service (KNS) Director Meteorological Centre Srinagar, Dr Mukhtar Ahmad, said an initial Western Disturbance was bringing light precipitation over isolated higher reaches, while the main weather activity was expected to begin in the early hours of November 12 and continue till the morning of November 14. "This is a significant weather system. While rainfall will dominate in the plains, we expect moderate snowfall across tourist places, marking the season's first snowfall in Doodhpathri, Pahalgam, Gulmarg and Sonamarg," Ahmad said. He said higher reaches and mountain passes, including Peer Ki Gali, Sinthan Top, Zojila, Razdan Pass, Sadhna Top and Margan Pass, were likely to receive heavy snowfall, with accumulations of one to two feet possible at some locations. The department has also indicated a 50 per cent possibility of light snowfall or mixed precipitation over the plains of Shopian, Kulgam, Kupwara, Bandipora and adjoining areas. In view of the forecast, the Bandipora district administration has temporarily prohibited tourists from visiting Gurez Valley and asked those already staying there to plan their departure immediately in coordination with the District Control Room. Candidates scheduled to appear in the Accounts Assistant written examination on November 15 have been advised to plan their journeys in advance and reach their examination centres before weather conditions deteriorate. The administration has also advised expectant mothers living in upper reaches, whose expected dates of delivery fall within the next month, to shift to nearby hospitals to ensure timely medical assistance in case snowfall disrupts road connectivity. Residents have been urged to avoid unnecessary travel towards Gurez and other higher reaches and refrain from organising social gatherings in vulnerable areas during the forecast period. Meanwhile, the Anantnag district administration has activated its District Emergency Operation Centre round the clock to deal with weather-related emergencies and public grievances. Departments, including Public Works (R&B), Mechanical Engineering, Revenue, Flood Control, PMGSY, Urban Local Bodies, KPDCL, Jal Shakti and Health and Medical Education, have been directed to take precautionary measures and keep manpower and machinery ready. The administration has issued helpline numbers 01932-227112, 9697982527, 7780885759 and 9419091681 for public assistance. The Meteorological Department has advised tourists, travellers and transporters to plan their journeys in advance, check road conditions before setting out and strictly follow traffic advisories. Farmers have also been advised to suspend harvesting operations on November 12 and 13 and ensure that harvested crops are safely stored to prevent damage from rain and snowfall. The fresh snowfall and the approaching weather system could affect traffic on several important mountain routes, including the Srinagar-Leh highway via Zojila, the Mughal Road and other high-altitude passes, the advisory said. (KNS)

stories.headline: India's GDP growth to beat RBI forecast? SBI sees 7.8% expansion in Q2; Moody's raises FY27 outlook
stories.title: India's GDP growth to beat RBI forecast? SBI sees 7.8% expansion in Q2; Moody's raises FY27 outlook
stories.summary: According to SBI Research, India's economic activity remained robust during July–September 2026, supported by manufacturing, services, corporate profitability and accelerating bank credit.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The research team used a dynamic factor model incorporating 54 high-frequency indicators to estimate second-quarter growth.
What is driving India's growth?
SBI Research noted that approximately 88% of 50 leading economic indicators showed acceleration in Q2 FY27, compared with 86% in the preceding quarter.
Manufacturing growth is projected at 8.7%, while services are expected to expand 9.7%, highlighting the continued strength of industrial and services activity.
Gross Value Added (GVA), which measures economic output across sectors, could grow between 8% and 8.2%.
Corporate earnings also indicate improving business conditions.
EBITDA and profit after tax of approximately 2,300 listed companies, excluding banking and financial services, increased 35% and 33%, respectively, year-on-year.
Bank lending remained another important growth driver.
Scheduled commercial bank credit growth accelerated to 18.2%, while deposit growth reached 16.7% for the fortnight ended October 15.
SBI Research also expects nominal GDP growth of 11–11.5% in the September quarter.
Separately, Moody's Ratings upgraded India's FY27 economic growth projection to 7% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

"India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," Moody's said in its Global Macro Outlook 2027–28.
